node_notes.button: The BUTTON_0 part-driver interface is initialized, given a pressed-event callback, and enabled by the application. Those calls are in application/main.c; no physical pin mapping is established in the provided files.
node_notes.led: The application turns on and toggles the MX_STATUS_LED through the LED part driver. These operations appear in application/main.c, but the provided evidence does not establish the part's physical pin mapping.
node_notes.logger: This utility supplies the LOGI macro used by the app and expands it to printf. The macro definitions and stdio include are in firmware/utils/logger/logger.h.
node_notes.main: This application entry point initializes the button interface, handles its event flag, and controls the status LED. The evidence is the button and LED driver calls plus app_start in application/main.c.
node_notes.console: This is the destination for direct printf calls and the logger's printf-backed output after mx_basic_stdio_init. The console initialization and logging calls appear in application/main.c, while the logger macro implementation is in firmware/utils/logger/logger.h.
node_notes.usart: The project brief identifies a USART UART device as the console transport. The supplied source does not identify its USART instance or TX/RX pin bindings.
node_notes.app: This firmware hook logs that the firmware has started when main calls app_start. Its implementation uses LOGI in firmware/app/app.c, and that macro is backed by printf in firmware/utils/logger/logger.h.

node_notes.buttoninit: The code retrieves the BUTTON_0 object and initializes it, returning on failure. Both operations are in application/main.c.
node_notes.ledon: The application sets the status LED on as its initial state. The call is in application/main.c and uses MX_STATUS_LED.
node_notes.buttonenable: Button event generation is enabled before the application begins monitoring the event flag. The button_enableit call is in application/main.c.
node_notes.toggle: After clearing the flag, the loop toggles the status LED and prints a message. Both operations are in application/main.c.
node_notes.callbackreg: The application registers ButtonCb for BUTTON_EVENT_PRESSED and stops startup if registration fails. This registration is in application/main.c.
node_notes.stdio: The application initializes basic stdio before emitting console output. The call and its failure check are in application/main.c.
node_notes.appstart: The application calls the firmware hook after board-interface setup and startup messages. The hook implementation is firmware/app/app.c.
node_notes.start: The application first requests system initialization and returns an error if it fails. This call is in application/main.c before console or button setup.
node_notes.callback: The registered button callback sets EventFlag to 1 to notify the main loop of a pressed event. Its implementation is ButtonCb in application/main.c.
node_notes.clearstart: The event flag is cleared and startup/readiness messages are printed before LED and firmware startup. This setup is in application/main.c.
node_notes.clear: On a detected event, the loop clears EventFlag so a later button press can be observed. This assignment is in application/main.c.
node_notes.poll: The main loop checks whether EventFlag is 1 and otherwise keeps polling. This branch is in application/main.c; the source specifies no polling period.

sequence.title: Sequence Diagram
sequence.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Main as application/main.c
  participant Button as BUTTON_0 driver
  participant LED as MX_STATUS_LED driver
  participant App as firmware/app/app.c
  participant Console as printf console
  participant USART as UART device
  Main->>Main: mx_system_init
  Main->>Console: mx_basic_stdio_init
  Main->>Button: mx_button_0_getobject and button_init
  Main->>Button: button_register_callback for BUTTON_EVENT_PRESSED
  Main->>Button: button_enableit
  Main->>LED: led_on
  Main->>App: app_start
  App->>Console: LOGI firmware started via printf
  Console->>USART: UART console output
  loop Main continuously polls EventFlag
    alt ButtonCb set EventFlag to 1
      Button-->>Main: BUTTON_EVENT_PRESSED
      Main->>LED: led_toggle
      Main->>Console: printf LED toggled
      Console->>USART: UART console output
    else No button event pending
      Main->>Main: Continue polling
    end
  end
